mechanism_inventory: missing sender/source validation in sgReceive (permissionless payload injection)
wrong value used for minimum received amount (SG_FEE_BPS constant misapplied)
stale/missing slippage check: minAmountLD derived from local constant not on-chain pool state
approval to wrong amount or wrong token in sgReceive (swapParams.amountIn vs actual amountLD received)
missing chain-of-origin validation: _srcChainId and _srcAddress ignored in sgReceive
missing invariant enforcement: no cap or sanity check on amt2Bridge relative to balance
external-call failure / DoS: IERC20.transferFrom in bridge can fail silently if return value not checked
hook caller / timing mismatch: onlyExecutor in sgReceive — what is the executor and is it trusted?
wrong variable used: sgReceive approves swapParams.amountIn (payload, attacker-controlled) instead of actual amountLD (on-chain received amount)

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: sgReceive ignores all cross-chain source validation parameters (_srcChainId, _srcAddress) — they are unnamed and discarded. The only guard is onlyExecutor, which restricts who can call sgReceive on-chain but does NOT validate which source chain or source contract sent the message. An attacker can craft an arbitrary payload and trigger arbitrary UTB execution with attacker-controlled postBridge, target, paymentOperator, utbPayload, refund.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any address satisfying onlyExecutor (or the Stargate executor if permissionless) calls sgReceive with a crafted payload encoding arbitrary target, paymentOperator, utbPayload, and a malicious postBridge.swapPayload.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker calls sgReceive(any_src_chain, any_src_address, any_nonce, any_token, any_amountLD, crafted_payload) if onlyExecutor allows. 2. sgReceive decodes payload entirely from attacker bytes. 3. IERC20(swapParams.tokenIn).approve(utb, swapParams.amountIn) with attacker-chosen token/amount. 4. IUTB(utb).receiveFromBridge(...) with attacker-chosen target/paymentOperator/utbPayload/refund — arbitrary execution in UTB context against adapter-held tokens.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: StargateBridgeAdapter approved token balances; users with in-flight funds; UTB balances drained via arbitrary swaps.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker gains tokens drained from adapter or UTB.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: _srcChainId and _srcAddress are explicitly unnamed (discarded) — no source validation. Primary critical mechanism: even if onlyExecutor restricts direct callers, absence of source-chain validation means any legitimate executor can relay a forged cross-chain message.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: sgReceive approves swapParams.amountIn (decoded from untrusted payload) to utb, not the actual amountLD (real amount received from Stargate). Approval amount is fully attacker-controlled via the payload; an attacker can set amountIn arbitrarily large, approving more than was bridged.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any entity controlling the bridgePayload sets postBridge.swapPayload with swapParams.amountIn >> actual bridged amount.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. sgReceive arrives with payload where swapParams.amountIn=large. 2. approve(utb, large). 3. receiveFromBridge processes inflated amountIn. 4. UTB pulls large tokens from adapter (if held) or the approval enables future pull, draining adapter beyond what was bridged.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: StargateBridgeAdapter token holders; in-flight users; protocol liquidity.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker or manipulative sender gains excess tokens.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Distinct wrong-variable bug: amountLD is verified on-chain, swapParams.amountIn is payload-supplied unverified — different variables/accounting paths; independently allows value extraction.
